summary: Sep. 8 Atlas ISR catch-up: five additional Iranian tanker losses, Iranian Jordan missile attack, Houthi Saudi energy attacks, U.S./UK sanctions, Gulf/China/Russia diplomacy, South Korea assessment and U.S. Dive-LD loss.

events.summary: CENTCOM said U.S. forces struck and rendered five Iranian crude carriers inoperable—Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, Riesco and Derya—after the IRGC targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over two days. Crews were directed to abandon ship first.
events.adjudication_note: Five vessels are durable commercial/shadow-fleet losses; IRGC financing allegations do not convert them into military platforms.

events.summary: Iran launched 20 ballistic missiles toward a U.S.-used base near Al Azraq, Jordan. Jordan said 18 were intercepted, two fell in unpopulated areas and no casualties occurred. Iranian claims of heavy damage were not independently established.
events.adjudication_note: Attack and interception count are supported by Jordanian reporting; heavy-damage claim remains separate.

events.summary: Houthi missile/drone attacks struck Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran, wounded 73 civilians and caused fires and operational disruption at Saudi energy facilities.
events.adjudication_note: Houthi responsibility is supported. Direct Iranian operational command is not inferred.

events.summary: U.S. Treasury sanctioned 36 Iran aviation-sector targets, including 27 Iranian airlines, foreign intermediaries and procurement/transshipment networks, and suspended three Iran-related aviation authorizations.
events.adjudication_note: Records enacted U.S. sanctions action and authorization suspensions.

events.summary: The UK laid legislation to broaden Iran-related financial, trade, shipping and aviation restrictions, including additional sectoral measures linked to nuclear and other hostile activity.
events.adjudication_note: Legislation was laid on Sep. 8; measures with later effective dates are not treated as already in force at this cutoff.

events.summary: South Korea sent an assessment team to the UAE and discussed possible contributions to Hormuz maritime security, while stating no troop-deployment decision had been made.
events.adjudication_note: Assessment and policy review only; do not record military deployment.

events.summary: Qatar's prime minister/foreign minister met China's Wang Yi in Beijing and discussed de-escalation, security and freedom of navigation in Hormuz, and a comprehensive diplomatic agreement.
events.adjudication_note: Public diplomatic engagement is established; no Chinese material rescue commitment is inferred.

events.summary: An Arab League Council statement rejected Iranian fees under any designation, unilateral regulatory or supervisory authority over Hormuz, and attacks on commercial vessels, while calling for immediate restoration of freedom of navigation.
events.adjudication_note: Regional political/legal position; does not itself determine ultimate legal adjudication.

events.summary: Russian and Saudi foreign ministers discussed de-escalation and stressed security and freedom of navigation in Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb.
events.adjudication_note: Visible Russian posture in this interval was diplomatic; no new public material rescue package for Iran is established by this event.

events.summary: A U.S. Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle came into Iranian possession near Hormuz. The Pentagon acknowledged the loss and attributed it to a malfunction of an older model without classified systems or data; Anduril confirmed the incident.
events.adjudication_note: Physical loss/possession is supported; a combat defeat or successful Iranian technical exploitation is not established.

record.notes: Saudi authorities reported 73 civilians wounded, including women and children.
Jordanian armed forces explicitly reported no casualties after intercepting 18 of 20 missiles.

record.objective: Freedom of navigation and rejection of unilateral Iranian toll/control claims
record.evidence: Arab League Council rejected fees under any designation and unilateral Iranian regulatory/supervisory authority; UAE separately accelerated alternative routes and Qatar reiterated freedom-of-navigation demands.

record.deception_basis: Sep. 8 produced a materially wider retaliation cycle, but one short interval does not establish a durable repeatable doctrine or knowing deception.

CENTCOM's Sep. 8 account said all IRGC attempts against U.S. Navy warships had failed and no Americans were harmed in the latest attempts. No independent damage evidence supporting the Sep. 5 claim was established. Internal claimant knowledge remains unproven.

narrative_claims.claim: Iran claimed its ballistic-missile attack caused heavy damage at the U.S.-used base near Al Azraq, Jordan.
narrative_claims.proposition: The Sep. 8 Iranian missile attack caused heavy physical or functional damage at the targeted U.S.-used base.
narrative_claims.deception_basis: Jordan reported 18 of 20 missiles intercepted, two falling in unpopulated areas and no casualties; no independent heavy-damage evidence was established at cutoff. That does not establish the claimant's internal knowledge state.

narrative_claims.claim: The IRGC announced that it captured a U.S. Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle near Hormuz.
narrative_claims.proposition: Iran obtained physical possession of a U.S. Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle near Hormuz.
narrative_claims.deception_basis: The Pentagon acknowledged the loss and Anduril confirmed the incident. U.S. reporting attributes the loss to malfunction; possession is supported while a combat seizure/defeat is not established.
